newsitem.title: USA: Dow Industrials lower at midday.
newsitem.headline: Dow Industrials lower at midday.

text.p: A weak bond market and a sell-off in shares of Procter & Gamble Co pushed the Dow Industrials sharply lower at midday.
The Dow was down 40 points, or 0.66 percent, at 5997. Declines led advancing issues by four to three on moderate volume of 174 million shares.
The long bond was down 16/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The bond market sold off this morning when weekly jobless claims came in at 320,000, indicating the economy may be more robust than had been thought.

"Bonds are unhappy about the strong employment statistics which, combined with better retail activity as expressed in same-store sales over the past few weeks, seems to be indicating to the bond market that the economy in the fourth quarter will be stronger than it was in the third quarter," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.

"Things are not slowing down. In the long run, this means better earnings, which is something the market will benefit from. But what (the bond market) is really worried about now is the Federal Reserve, which may have to think about raising rates next year."
He said the stock market has had a strong run and that the concerns now arising are a good opportunity for investors to take profits.
A special weight in the Dow came from Procter & Gamble, which tumbled 3-1/2 to 92-3/4 after reporting higher fiscal first quarter earnings this morning.
Wesley Roberts, who covers the company for JJB Hilliard, LW Lyons, said his initial impression was that the stock was off "probably because the top line was pretty weak."

Procter & Gamble said that despite record unit sales worldwide, its sales for the quarter slipped to $8.90 billion from $9.03 billion a year earlier, primarily because of the strong dollar compared with other currencies.
Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities, said the market was beginning to show wear and tear, which was evident in diminishing volume.
"The volume level is not the same as it was earlier in the year. That comes from pushing to new highs" Nie said. "We don't seem to be able to create robust volume on the upside."
He said there was a lack of investment demand.
"I think we are looking at the end of an up-phase, to be followed by a minor move down to work off the overbought condition," Nie said.
Better support on the Dow will be found at the 5600/5700 level over the next two to four weeks, he said.
"We're not entering a bear market," he said. "At these levels the overall volume is insufficient to keep the market levitated. We are vulnerable."
Among special situations, Dell Computer was up 2-1/2 at 85 after Merrill Lynch raised its estimates to $4.60 a share from $4.30 for 1997, and to $6 from $5.10 for 1998.
Electronic Arts Inc was up 4-5/16 at 37-11/16 after Alex. Brown raised its rating on the stock to buy from neutral.
The high techs continued their rally from Wednesday, pushing the Nasdaq Composite Index up more than three points, or 0.28 percent, to 1231.
Microsoft Corp was up 2-1/4 at 136-3/4 and Intel Corp rose one to 110-3/8.
-- Wall Street Desk 212-859-1737
